title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
slides: Data centers are undoing clean air gains—how bad?
Diesel generators power the AI boom's backup systems
Emissions spike in communities near these facilities
Local air quality monitors may miss this pollution
Check your region's data center plans before approving
thread_text:
1. The Hidden Cost of AI

Backup diesel generators at data centers run far more than emergency use—often hundreds of hours a year. That exhaust is drifting into nearby neighborhoods.

2. The Diesel Problem

These generators aren't just for outages. They're increasingly used for grid support and peak shaving, meaning they fire up regularly—not rarely.

3. Monitors Miss the Mark

Many local air quality stations are placed away from data centers. So official readings show 'clean' even when residents are breathing diesel exhaust.

4. Health in the Crosshairs

Fine particulate matter from diesel is linked to asthma, heart attacks, and premature death. Communities near these facilities face elevated risks that aren't being tracked.

5. Check Before You Approve

Find your region's data center proposals and ask: where are the generators, how often will they run, and who's monitoring the air? Do it before the next vote.
